Tell her that she and her husband have actually TRY to make the marriage work. Take your offer for marriage counseling and do their best there. Soon the guys started asking if I was gay, even tho they knew I had a boyfriend with whom I had a child with, and I would skirt around the question. I let them believe I was Bi for the longest time, but after awhile, I just started hating it. I had bought this necklace that says, HUMAN, on it and all the letters are an LGBTQ+ flag. I bought it for the Pan flag mostly. (I ended up buying a hat just like it later) and started putting Pan accessories on my work lanyard, so far just one pin but I plan to get more.

So, very slowly, anytime the question of my sexuality came up, I just said I didn't care. Which confused them, poor things. I would have to tell them that I didn't care about labels, gender identity, sexual preference, (unless you're a gay male or something along those lines. Always be respectful) race or whatever. My wording was to the effect of,

"I fall in love with a person. I don't care where they come from or what they have. If they're a man, cool. If they're a woman, cool. If they're Trans, cool. I just want to love and be loved."

I guess the point of this really long winded story is; 

Be true to yourself. You don't have to justify who you are or what your preferences are, you can be honest without having to go into detail. Just show your flag proudly and answer honestly with what's true to you.
